title: Quarterly Impact Deck — ROI & Risk Framework (Standard + Enterprise Variants)
content:
Purpose:
To provide a compact, impact-first QBR deck template that connects executive-level ROI with technical risk posture. This doc contains two parallel variants: Standard (customer-facing, outcome-oriented) and Enterprise (includes technical appendix and compliance callouts). Use as a starting deck for customers at renewal windows or major adoption milestones.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (owner)
- Account Executives (co-present)
- Solutions/SEs (Enterprise variant appendix owner)
- Customer exec sponsors and technical leads

How to use this template (quick guide):
1) Populate the Executive Summary with the single most important business outcome (one sentence).
2) Fill the ROI slide with actual customer metrics (savings, time-to-value, throughput improvements) — use conservative estimates.
3) Populate Risk Heatmap with active issues and mitigation status.
4) For Enterprise variant, attach the Architecture & Compliance appendix and circulate 48 hours before the meeting.

Deck Flow (slide-by-slide with speaker notes):
1) Title / Meeting Info
   - Slide: Customer name, date, participants, meeting objective (1 line)
   - Notes: Set expectations: "30 minutes + 10 for technical Q&A"

2) One-line Executive Impact (1 slide)
   - Slide: "What changed in the past quarter?" (3 bullets: result, driver, ask)
   - Notes: Lead with business outcomes, not features. Example: "Reduced per-call inference cost by 31% via batching, enabling 2x more active users."

3) Health Snapshot (1 slide)
   - Slide: Key metrics panel: active routes, avg latency, error rate, token volume, cost per 1K tokens, NPS trend
   - Notes: Call out any anomalies with a short root-cause pointer and current status

4) Adoption & Expansion Opportunities (1 slide)
   - Slide: New use-cases adopted, feature adoption (streaming, tools), roadmap match
   - Notes: Highlight quick wins and low-effort expansion plays

5) ROI & Cost Impact (2 slides)
   - Slide A: Quantified savings (baseline vs current), productivity gains, user engagement increases
   - Slide B: Unit economics table (per-token cost breakdown, caching impact, batching efficiency)
   - Notes: Use actual billing + logs. If numbers are estimates, mark them clearly.

6) Risk Heatmap & Mitigations (1–2 slides)
   - Slide: 3x3 heatmap: Likelihood (low/med/high) vs Impact (low/med/high) with short owner tags
   - Notes: For each high-impact/high-likelihood item show mitigation due dates and owner

7) Renewal Health & Recommendation (1 slide)
   - Slide: Renewal status (green/yellow/red), proposed commercial ask (standard or upsell), timeline
   - Notes: Be explicit: recommended renewal tier, required exec commitment, any discounting guardrails

8) 30/60/90 Success Plan (1 slide)
   - Slide: Milestones, owners, success criteria, KPIs to track post-renewal
   - Notes: Keep items specific and measurable

9) Ask & Decision Points (1 slide)
   - Slide: Top 2 asks (contract + technical approval), any required internal approvals and dates
   - Notes: End with a clear "Yes/No/Need more info" ask with next steps mapped out

Enterprise Appendix (separate file or final slides — required for enterprise customers):
A) Architecture Snapshot
   - Slide: Logical diagram of inference path, data flows, integrations (webhooks, VPC, KMS)
   - Notes: Include SLOs per component (latency, throughput) and current observed values

B) Compliance & Data Residency
   - Slide: Map of data ingress/egress, storage zones, encryption in transit/at rest, required certifications (SOC2, ISO) and current posture
   - Notes: If gaps exist, state remediation plan and timelines

C) Performance & Capacity Plan
   - Slide: Per-route throughput baselines, peak observed QPS, tail latency percentiles, expected growth curve
   - Notes: Include recommended Dedicated capacity profiles or burst plan if appropriate

D) Incident & Change History (last 90 days)
   - Slide: Short timeline of incidents, root causes, fixes, outstanding actions

Renewal Tracker (lightweight template to paste into tracker sheet):
Columns: Account | Renewal Date | Renewal Owner | Current SKU | Proposed SKU | ARR at Renewal | Health (G/Y/R) | Open Risks | Technical Owner | Next Action | Last Contact
Example row: "Acme Corp | 2025-05-15 | Priya Kaur | Hosted-Pro | Dedicated-1 | $180,000 | Y | Peak latency spikes | Marcus Patel | Send SOW draft | 2025-02-25"

Pre-QBR checklist (recommended):
- Verify metrics (billing, latency, errors) with infra logs (owner: CS Analyst)
- Run a 15-min pre-brief with AE + SE (owner: CSM)
- Send Enterprise appendix to technical contacts 48h before (owner: SE)
- Confirm executive attendees and pre-meet ask (owner: AE)
- Attach 1-pager ROI snapshot to calendar invite (owner: CSM)

Post-QBR follow-up template (email bullets):
- Thank you + one-sentence summary of outcome
- List of agreed next steps with owners and dates
- Attach updated SOW/revision or renewal quote
- Request confirmation on decision timeline

Playbook: handling a yellow/red renewal
- Yellow: escalate to AE to schedule executive-to-executive 15-min sync; propose targeted POA (proof-of-action) for 30-day recovery; offer technical office hours
- Red: open cross-functional war-room (CS Lead, AE, SE, Eng on-call). Prepare remediation runbook and show measurable improvements before renewal date. Set at least weekly checkpoints

Tone & Presentation tips:
- Start with business outcomes not platform features.
- Use conservative, verifiable numbers.
- When presenting risks, always attach mitigation and owner.
- For enterprise audiences, add a 1–2 slide technical Q&A slot after the main deck

Editable assets to keep in the shared folder (suggested):
- Slide master for "Impact-first QBR" (Google Slides)
- CSV renewal tracker template
- One-page ROI calculator (sheet)
- Enterprise appendix template (pptx)

Open questions / TODOs for this draft:
- Decide default renewal ask language for mid-market vs enterprise (AE input needed)
- Add sample anonymized ROI calculations for 3 typical buyer profiles
- Create slide library of small visuals (heatmap, cost waterfall, architecture stencil)

Notes to the author:
- This is intentionally outcome-first to differentiate from feature-heavy decks.
- Keep the Enterprise appendix modular so it can be appended or handed to engineering-only sessions.

Revision history:
- 2025-02-12: Initial draft (Priya Kaur)
- 2025-02-20: Added Renewal Tracker sample & pre-QBR checklist (Ethan Morales)
- 2025-02-28: Enterprise appendix outline and compliance bullets (Jade Lin)

End of document.
